items.title: Core Mission and Functions
items.content: ICQA (Inventory Control and Quality Assurance) executes count processes as an audit mechanism to identify and correct inventory defects. Responsibilities include inventory management programs, defect reduction, reporting, and process improvement.

items.title: Why Counting Matters
items.content: Counting ensures inventory accuracy, improves quality, supports operational planning, mitigates risks, and ensures SOX compliance.

items.title: Simple Bin Count (SBC)
items.content: Counts all items in a tote. Lowest priority. Used to identify quantity defects. Does not update inventory records.

items.title: Cycle Count (CC)
items.content: Scans every item and ASIN. Medium priority. Can update inventory. Requires agreement between two associates.

items.title: Inventory Record Defect Rate (IRDR)
items.content: Measures accuracy between physical and virtual inventory. Target is ≤15,000 DPMO.

items.title: DIPCH
items.content: Defects Identified Per Count Hour. Measures effectiveness of SBC in identifying defects.

items.title: RCPCH
items.content: Records Cleaned Per Count Hour. Measures how effective count hours are at cleaning defects.

items.title: SOX Compliance
items.content: Ensures accurate financial reporting and requires strict auditing of inventory adjustments.

items.title: TOAD System
items.content: AI-based system that predicts which bins are likely to contain defects to improve counting efficiency.

items.title: Stoat Model
items.content: Machine learning model that powers TOAD by analyzing bin-level inventory data.
